correctness.rationale: The star Laplacian has the constants, the hub-against-leaves vector and the leaf-zero-sum space as mutually orthogonal eigenspaces with eigenvalues 0, n+1 and 1. The added Laplacian vanishes on the first two and has trace 2T and rank at most k on the last. Padding with zeros, the improvement is the sum of f(mu)=mu/(1+mu) at k spectral values. Jensen and strict monotonicity in T give the optimum and require T=W and mu_i=2W/k for every i. Thus exactly k edges are positive and the incidence Gram matrix must be (2W/k)I: its diagonals require equal weights and its off-diagonals force disjointness. Such a matching exists by 2k<=n, including n=2. The curvature lower bound for -f on [0,2W] gives an objective deficit at least the spectral squared deviation divided by (1+2W)^3. The latter squared deviation is the squared Frobenius deviation of the Gram matrix even when rank is deficient; its diagonals give 4 times the weight variance sum, and the two orientations of each off-diagonal give twice the stated overlap sum. Multiplying by n+1 gives the stated Kirchhoff index.
residual_risks: The explicit gap bound assumes k positive weights and full budget; it does not claim the best possible coefficient. The finite computations are not a proof over the continuum of weights.

evidence: Bhoite et al. model a weighted base graph with coupled cardinality and conductance budget and propose an SDP relaxation, rounding and greedy heuristics. Ghosh et al. allocate conductance on prescribed edge vectors and include uniform conductances on the original star. Kooij–Achterberg treat a general unweighted augmentation complexity problem.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The base-star spoke weights are fixed in the finding and the leaf support is part of the optimizer. A numerical general framework, optimizing spokes on a prescribed star, or a hardness theorem does not imply the closed global value, all minimizers or the lower bound on deviation.

value.rationale: A hub-and-spoke network with sparse new links and fixed conductance resources is a natural instance of a nonconvex design problem. The solution specifies when the continuous budget and the combinatorial optimum can be realized simultaneously, and turns strict inequality into a directly interpretable penalty for support overlap and unequal weights. This is useful beyond the known one-unit-link calculation or restating the general design objective.
residual_risks: Availability of a k-matching and fixed equal spokes are essential to this proof; the result does not solve general graph augmentation.
